「この機会を一時のブームで［54］」と、関係者はいろいろなアイデアを出している。

studyExplanation.translation: People involved are trying many ideas because they do not want this opportunity to end as a temporary fad.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 終わらせまい (owarasemai) - determined not to let it end

choices.reason: 終わらせたい means want to end it, opposite to the effort to sustain interest in go.
終わらせよう means let us end it, again opposite to the ideas being proposed.
The negative volitional まい expresses a firm intention not to let the opportunity end as a passing boom.
終わりたくない means do not want to end, but the people are trying not to let the boom end; the causative 終わらせまい fits their active prevention.

sets.title: 第2回 模擬テスト
sets.description: 第2回　文字・語彙・文法

questions.questionText: ネット環境が整えばオフィスに<u>縛られる</u>ことなく、どこにいても仕事ができる。
questions.instruction: 問題1　下線の言葉の読み方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: If an internet connection is available, people can work anywhere without being tied to an office.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: shibarareru - to be bound or restricted

choices.reason: Hamerareru means to be fitted into something or trapped; it is not the reading of the written verb meaning to be bound.
Osamerareru can mean to be contained or brought under control, but the written verb here is read shibarareru.
Torareru means to be taken; it neither reads the written verb nor conveys being tied to an office.
The verb is read shibarareru; here it figuratively means being constrained to work in an office.

questions.questionText: 電車の中は、たくさんの子どもが乗っていて<u>騒々</u>しかった。
questions.instruction: 問題1　下線の言葉の読み方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: The train was noisy because many children were riding in it.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: souzou - noisy or boisterous (in souzoushii)

choices.reason: Souzoushii means noisy or boisterous, fitting the crowded train.
Zuuzuu is associated with shamelessly pushy behavior, as in zuuzuushii, not the reading of this word.
Araara is not the reading of the characters in souzoushii.
Imaima belongs to imaimashii, meaning irritating or detestable, not this noisy-train adjective.

questions.questionText: 我が社は今年から面接の回数を増やして、知識より人物<u>重視</u>で社員を採用する。
questions.instruction: 問題1　下線の言葉の読み方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Starting this year, our company will conduct more interviews and hire employees with greater emphasis on character than on knowledge.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: juushi - emphasis or prioritization

choices.reason: Choushi can mean condition or tone, but the compound for placing importance on something is juushi.
Neither character in this compound is read as chouji here.
Shuuji is a different reading and does not name the act of prioritizing character in hiring.
Juushi means placing importance on something; jinbutsu juushi is emphasis on applicants' character.

questions.questionText: お買い物でためたポイントは、商品券に<u>交換</u>できます。
questions.instruction: 問題1　下線の言葉の読み方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: You can exchange the points you earned while shopping for gift certificates.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: koukan - exchange

choices.reason: Koukan means exchange; points can be exchanged for gift certificates.
Both syllables are wrong for this compound: the first begins with k and the second is kan, not gan.
The first half is right, but the second character is kan, not gan.
The second half is right, but the first character is kou, not gou.

questions.questionText: スーパーでは食品の<u>包装</u>を少なくする活動が進んでいる。
questions.instruction: 問題1　下線の言葉の読み方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Supermarkets are moving ahead with efforts to reduce food packaging.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: housou - packaging

choices.reason: The first syllable is right, but the second character is sou, not zou.
The second half is right, but the first character is hou, not bou.
Housou means wrapping or packaging, the material supermarkets are trying to reduce.
Both syllables are voiced incorrectly for this packaging compound.

questions.questionText: 太陽エネルギーが生み出す熱は<u>だんぼう</u>に、光は電気に利用できる。
questions.instruction: 問題2　下線の言葉を漢字で書くとき、最もよいものを1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: The heat produced by solar energy can be used for heating, while its light can be used for electricity.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: danbou - heating; written with the characters for warmth and room

choices.reason: These are the standard characters for indoor heating: warmth plus room.
The second character means to risk or wear a crown, not a room; it does not spell heating.
The first character means to cut off, not warmth, so this is not the heating compound.
Both characters are wrong for heating: it needs warmth and room, not cutting off and risking.

questions.questionText: あの2人は夫婦だと<u>かんちがい</u>している人が多い。
questions.instruction: 問題2　下線の言葉を漢字で書くとき、最もよいものを1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Many people mistakenly think those two are a married couple.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: kanchigai - misunderstanding or mistaken belief

choices.reason: The first character denotes intuition or a hunch; together the word means a mistaken assumption.
The first character means liver, not the character used in the word for misunderstanding.
This uses the character for feeling instead of the one used in the established word kanchigai.
The first character means to block or stuff; it does not form the word for a mistaken assumption.

questions.questionText: 常識に<u>てらして</u>考えてみれば、君が今、何をすべきかわかるだろう。
questions.instruction: 問題2　下線の言葉を漢字で書くとき、最もよいものを1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: If you consider it in light of common sense, you should understand what you ought to do now.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: terashite - in light of, or by comparing with

choices.reason: The first character means to be impatient or burn; the idiom for judging by a standard uses the character for illuminating.
This uses an incorrect character associated with burning; it is not the written form of terashite.
Terashite means illuminate or compare against; comparing something with common sense is the intended idiom.
The character for fierce fire is not used in the idiom meaning to judge in light of a standard.

questions.questionText: このあたりは地震で<u>じばん</u>が沈んでしまった。
questions.instruction: 問題2　下線の言葉を漢字で書くとき、最もよいものを1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: The ground in this area sank because of the earthquake.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: jiban - ground or geological foundation

choices.reason: The second character means a site or layout, not the ground or geological base.
The second character means a printing plate or edition; it does not denote the ground.
This compound refers to a land-lot number, not the ground that can sink in an earthquake.
The second character denotes a base or foundation; this is the standard word for ground conditions.

questions.questionText: 工場の事故で有害物質が流れ、川が<u>おせん</u>された。
questions.instruction: 問題2　下線の言葉を漢字で書くとき、最もよいものを1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Harmful substances flowed out in a factory accident and polluted the river.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: osen - pollution or contamination

choices.reason: The second character means wash, not dye or stain; this is not the word for pollution.
The first character means govern or honorific prefix, not dirt; it cannot express contamination here.
The characters mean dirty and stain; osen is environmental contamination.
The first character means risk or adventure, not dirt; it is not the standard pollution compound.

questions.questionText: インドのガンジーは（　）暴力を信条に独立運動を指導した。
questions.instruction: 問題3　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Gandhi of India led the independence movement with nonviolence as his guiding principle.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: hibouryoku - nonviolence

choices.reason: Mu means absence, but the established compound for nonviolence uses hi, not mu.
Han means opposition; it does not form the standard noun for the principle of nonviolence.
Hi negates the noun violence; hibouryoku is the fixed expression for nonviolence.
Fu is a negative prefix in other compounds, but the standard word here is hibouryoku.

questions.questionText: 山田氏は、個性（　）俳優として活躍している。
questions.instruction: 問題3　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Mr. Yamada is active as an actor with a distinctive personality.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: koseiha - a distinctive or individualistic type (of actor)

choices.reason: Adding the character for person does not form the usual label for an actor known for individuality.
The character for style or wind does not complete the fixed expression koseiha.
The character for school or style does not make the established compound for an individualistic actor.
The suffix ha means a type or school; koseiha describes a distinctive, individualistic performer.

questions.questionText: 全社員に職場の改善（　）を聞く。
questions.instruction: 問題3　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Ask all employees which aspects of the workplace need improvement.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: kaizen-ten - points for improvement

choices.reason: Ten means point or aspect; kaizen-ten are specific points that can be improved.
The character for opinion does not form the standard compound for points needing improvement.
The character for place does not turn improvement into a list of aspects to ask employees about.
The character for location does not make the idiomatic expression kaizen-ten.

questions.questionText: 自然（　）の法則には逆らえない。
questions.instruction: 問題3　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: We cannot defy the laws of the natural world.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: shizenkai - the natural world

choices.reason: This character means direction or side, but it does not form the established phrase for the natural world.
This character means side, not the world or realm governed by nature's laws.
Kai means realm or world; shizenkai is the natural world and can have laws.
This character means generation or world in other contexts, but shizensei is not the phrase here.

questions.questionText: 子どもたちは（　）年齢とあって、すぐに仲よくなった。
questions.instruction: 問題3　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Because the children were the same age, they quickly became friends.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: dounenrei - the same age

choices.reason: Kin means near; the sentence specifies children of the same age, expressed with dou.
Dou means same; dounenrei means being of the same age, which explains why they bonded quickly.
Nan means what; it does not express a shared age in the causal phrase to atte.
Tou means corresponding or applicable; it does not form the standard expression for the same age.

questions.questionText: サークルのホームページに「イベント情報」を追加し、（　）した。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: I added an 'Event Information' page to the club website and updated it.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: koushin - update or renew

choices.reason: Seisaku means create or produce; the website already existed and was updated with new information.
Kouji means construction work, usually physical work, not updating a website's content.
Heisa means closure; adding event information is the opposite of closing the site.
Koushin means update; adding a new page changes the existing website.

questions.questionText: 最も（　）な成績の学生には、大学から学長賞が贈られます。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: The university presents a president's award to the student with the most outstanding grades.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: yuushuu - outstanding or excellent

choices.reason: Joutou means high quality or first-rate, but it is not the natural description of a student's academic performance here.
Yuushuu describes excellent performance or ability, and pairs naturally with grades.
Yuukou means effective or valid; grades can be excellent, not effective.
Yuuryou can mean good or high quality, but yuushuu is the idiomatic superlative description of outstanding grades.

questions.questionText: 買い物という日常的な行いが、消費を（　）して世の中を元気にする。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: The everyday act of shopping stimulates consumption and revitalizes society.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: shigeki - stimulate

choices.reason: Juushi means prioritize or emphasize; shopping affects consumption rather than merely emphasizing it.
Shidou means guide or instruct, usually people or activities, not consumption itself.
Katsuyou means make practical use of something; buying goods stimulates demand instead.
Shigeki means stimulate; everyday purchases encourage further consumption.

questions.questionText: バスがなかなか来なくて、待っている人たちは次第に（　）し始めた。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: The bus did not come for a long time, and the people waiting gradually became irritated.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: iraira - irritated or impatient

choices.reason: Iraira describes mounting irritation from waiting too long for the bus.
Butsubutsu means muttering or grumbling aloud; the sentence describes a growing feeling of impatience.
Noronoro describes slow movement, not the waiters' emotional reaction.
Magomago means being confused or at a loss, not irritated by a delayed bus.

questions.questionText: 日本の寿司を（　）した洋風の寿司が海外で人気だ。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Western-style sushi adapted from Japanese sushi is popular overseas.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: arenji - adapt or modify an existing design

choices.reason: Approach means to move toward or tackle something, not modify sushi into a new style.
Arenji means to arrange or adapt an existing item; Western-style sushi is a modified version.
Assist means help someone, not change a food's style.
Advice is guidance given to a person, not an adaptation of sushi.

questions.questionText: 幸福が（　）に続くことはありえないのだろうか。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Is it impossible for happiness to last forever?
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: eien - forever, for eternity

choices.reason: Chouki means a long term; chouki ni tsuzuku is not the intended expression for lasting eternally.
Fuhen means unchanging, but fuhen ni tsuzuku is awkward here; the question asks about duration without end.
Eien ni tsuzuku means to continue forever, exactly the possibility the speaker questions.
Fumetsu means imperishable; it describes something that cannot be destroyed, rather than the adverbial duration of happiness here.

questions.questionText: あの大企業の社長は自分にはこれといった才能はないと（　）している。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: The president of that large company modestly says that he has no particular talent.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: kenson - modesty or speaking humbly of oneself

choices.reason: Kenson suru means to speak modestly of oneself; saying one has no special talent fits this.
Enryo suru means to hold back or refrain, not downplay one's own abilities in speech.
Hairyo suru means to show consideration for others, not describe oneself modestly.
Kyoushuku suru means to feel obliged or embarrassed by kindness; it is not the act of humble self-description.

questions.questionText: 試合に負けた悔しさを<u>味わった</u>。
questions.instruction: 問題5　下線の言葉に意味が最も近いものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: I experienced the frustration of losing the match.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: keiken shita - experienced; paraphrases ajiwatta, felt firsthand

choices.reason: Recording a result is not the same as personally feeling the frustration of defeat.
Announcing something publicly does not describe experiencing the feeling oneself.
Prioritizing something is not what ajiwatta means in the context of an emotion.
Experiencing something firsthand is the meaning of ajiwatta when the object is frustration.

questions.questionText: 旅先で<u>偶然</u>昔の友人に出会った。
questions.instruction: 問題5　下線の言葉に意味が最も近いものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: I unexpectedly met an old friend while traveling.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: omoigakenaku - unexpectedly; paraphrases guuzen, by chance

choices.reason: As promised implies a planned meeting, the opposite of meeting by chance.
Unexpectedly matches guuzen, a chance encounter with an old friend.
Certainly expresses confidence, not the unplanned nature of the meeting.
Conveniently expresses favorable timing, not necessarily chance or surprise.

questions.questionText: 工場の<u>単調な</u>作業にあきてきた。
questions.instruction: 問題5　下線の言葉に意味が最も近いものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: I have grown tired of the monotonous work at the factory.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: henka ga nai - unchanging; paraphrases tanchou na, monotonous

choices.reason: With no variation, the factory task is monotonous, which explains the boredom.
Changing frequently is the opposite of monotonous, repetitive work.
Taking effort or time does not mean lacking variety.
Having no break can be tiring, but it does not define monotonous work.

questions.questionText: 負けて困っているところに、<u>強力な</u>味方が現われた。
questions.instruction: 問題5　下線の言葉に意味が最も近いものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Just when we were struggling because we were losing, a powerful ally appeared.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: tayori ni naru - dependable; paraphrases kyouryoku na, powerful

choices.reason: Laid-back does not describe the strong assistance needed when losing.
Unexpected describes surprise, not the ally's helpful strength.
A reliable ally can provide strong help; this captures kyouryoku na in context.
Lively or energetic is not necessarily dependable or powerful as an ally.

questions.questionText: 彼は<u>バイリンガルだ</u>。
questions.instruction: 問題5　下線の言葉に意味が最も近いものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: He is bilingual.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: nikakokugo o hanasu - speaks two languages

choices.reason: Being internationally minded does not imply the ability to speak two languages.
Knowing many facts is different from being able to use two languages.
Bilingual means speaking two languages; this states that ability directly.
Dual citizenship is a legal status and does not itself mean bilingual ability.

questions.questionText: 反映
options: 彼は酒を飲むとすぐに本性を<u>反映</u>する。
隠していた事実がついに世間に<u>反映</u>されてしまった。
客の希望を<u>反映</u>して、配達のサービスを始めた。
黒のドレスは色白の女性の美しさを特に<u>反映</u>していた。
questions.correctOption: 客の希望を<u>反映</u>して、配達のサービスを始めた。
questions.instruction: 問題6　次の言葉の使い方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation: 【正解】3（客の希望を<u>反映</u>して、配達のサービスを始めた。）

studyExplanation.translation: Reflecting customers' wishes, the company started a delivery service.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: han'ei - reflect or incorporate wishes and opinions

choices.reason: Someone's true nature may emerge when drinking, but han'ei means to reflect or incorporate something, not reveal a hidden personality.
A concealed fact coming to light is revelation, not the incorporation of opinions or circumstances.
Customer requests are reflected in a new service; the requests shape the company's decision.
A dress may bring out someone's beauty, but this sentence uses the word as if it meant enhance; that is not its intended use here.

questions.questionText: ためいき
options: 話がおもしろくて<u>ためいき</u>が出た。
苦手な上司の声を聞いただけで、ぞっと<u>ためいき</u>が出る。
息子のひどい成績に母は思わず<u>ためいき</u>をついた。
プールに入る前に、<u>ためいき</u>をしてください。
questions.correctOption: 息子のひどい成績に母は思わず<u>ためいき</u>をついた。
questions.instruction: 問題6　次の言葉の使い方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation: 【正解】3（息子のひどい成績に母は思わず<u>ためいき</u>をついた。）

studyExplanation.translation: Seeing her son's terrible grades, the mother involuntarily sighed.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: tameiki - a sigh

choices.reason: An amusing story usually draws laughter, not a sigh of disappointment or fatigue.
Feeling a chill at the boss's voice calls for a shudder; the phrase with zotto is not the normal way to describe a sigh.
Tameiki o tsuku is the fixed expression for sighing; her son's poor grades provide the cause.
Before entering a pool one might take a deep breath, but a sigh is not the action being requested.

questions.questionText: 特殊
options: 動物には、人間にない<u>特殊</u>な能力を持つものが多い。
夜中に<u>特殊</u>な物音がして目が覚めた。
彼って<u>特殊</u>にもてるけど、どこがいいのかしらね。
今日は<u>特殊</u>にあなただけにプレゼントをあげます。
questions.correctOption: 動物には、人間にない<u>特殊</u>な能力を持つものが多い。
questions.instruction: 問題6　次の言葉の使い方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation: 【正解】1（動物には、人間にない<u>特殊</u>な能力を持つものが多い。）

studyExplanation.translation: Many animals have special abilities that humans do not possess.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: tokushu - special or distinctive

choices.reason: Tokushu na nouryoku naturally means a special ability; the animal has an ability humans lack.
A strange noise in the middle of the night is usually described as unusual or odd, not as a specialized ability or type.
Tokushu is not the adverb for 'especially popular'; it is primarily used for a special kind or property.
Giving a gift 'especially to you' calls for tokubetsu ni, not tokushu ni.

questions.questionText: 加速度
options: 授業は個々の生徒の能力に合った<u>加速度</u>で進める。
もう少し<u>加速度</u>をつけないと時間に遅れてしまう。
あの人とはなぜか話の<u>加速度</u>が合わない。
地上を離れた飛行機は一気に<u>加速度</u>を増した。
questions.correctOption: 地上を離れた飛行機は一気に<u>加速度</u>を増した。
questions.instruction: 問題6　次の言葉の使い方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation: 【正解】4（地上を離れた飛行機は一気に<u>加速度</u>を増した。）

studyExplanation.translation: After taking off, the airplane rapidly increased its acceleration.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: kasokudo - acceleration, the rate at which speed increases

choices.reason: The pace of a lesson is its speed or rate, not its physical acceleration.
To avoid being late one increases speed; acceleration is not the natural noun for this everyday instruction.
People can match conversational pace or tempo, not conversational acceleration.
An airplane speeding up after leaving the ground can increase acceleration; the word fits physical motion.

questions.questionText: <ruby>矛盾<rt>むじゅん</rt></ruby>
options: 私は工場建設に賛成の彼とは<u>矛盾</u>する立場にある。
2人は最初から最後まで<u>矛盾</u>ばかりだ。
税金は安くして行政サービスはよくしろだなんて、<u>矛盾</u>している。
やっぱり聞くことと見ることでは<u>矛盾</u>している。
questions.correctOption: 税金は安くして行政サービスはよくしろだなんて、<u>矛盾</u>している。
questions.instruction: 問題6　次の言葉の使い方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation: 【正解】3（税金は安くして行政サービスはよくしろだなんて、<u>矛盾</u>している。）

studyExplanation.translation: Demanding both lower taxes and better government services is contradictory.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: mujun - contradiction or inconsistency

choices.reason: Disagreeing with someone's position is opposition; this sentence does not present two logically inconsistent claims.
Two people disagreeing throughout a discussion would be in conflict; mujun is not normally used this way without specifying contradictory claims.
Lower taxes alongside better services creates conflicting demands; the ideas contradict each other.
Hearing and seeing can differ, but the sentence does not specify contradictory statements or facts.

questions.questionText: お金がない（　）ではないが、必要ないものは買わないことにしている。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】1（わけ）
「～ないわけではない（が）」⇒二重否定で「完全に～ないということではないが（少しは～である）」という意味を表す。

studyExplanation.translation: It is not that I have no money, but I have decided not to buy things I do not need.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: wake - reason or case; nai wake dewa nai means 'it is not that ... not'

choices.reason: Nai wake dewa nai is the fixed double-negative pattern: it is not the case that I lack money.
Nai koto dewa nai is not the intended idiom for denying the explanation that one lacks money.
Nai mono dewa nai does not make the textbook's explanatory double-negative pattern in this sentence.
Dokoro dewa nai means 'far from being a situation for'; it does not fit the existing nai before the blank.

questions.questionText: これから大急ぎで行った（　）、授業に間に合わないだろう。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】2（としても）
「～としても」⇒もし～しても〈「たとえ～ても」と同じ意味を表す。〉

studyExplanation.translation: Even if I hurry there from now, I probably will not make it to class on time.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: toshitemo - even if, supposing that

choices.reason: Toshitara sets up a condition, but the sentence needs an even-if concession despite hurrying.
Toshitemo means even if; hurrying will still not be enough to arrive on time.
Tosuruto introduces a consequence if the condition holds, not a result despite the effort.
Tonareba means if it comes to that situation; it does not express the required concessive contrast.

questions.questionText: 友人とおしゃべりをしている（　）、別の友人から電話がかかってきた。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】1（最中に）
「～（の）最中に」⇒ちょうど～しているとき〈ある程度の時間、継続して動作をしている途中でということを表す。【ex】食事の最中に〉

studyExplanation.translation: While I was chatting with a friend, another friend called me.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: saichuu ni - in the middle of an ongoing activity

choices.reason: Saichuu ni marks an interruption during the ongoing period of chatting.
Chokugo ni means immediately after, but the call occurred during the conversation.
Totan ni means the instant something happened; chatting is an ongoing activity, not a single moment of onset here.
Shunkan ni refers to an instant, whereas the sentence says the call came while chatting was in progress.

questions.questionText: この小さな絵が1億円もするなんて、（　）ですね。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】3（信じがたい）
「動詞ます形 + がたい」⇒～するのが難しい〈気持ちのうえで～できない、ということを表す。〉

studyExplanation.translation: It is hard to believe that this small painting costs as much as 100 million yen.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: shinjigatai - hard to believe

choices.reason: Kanenai means something may well happen, not that belief feels difficult.
Shika nai means there is no choice but to believe; that is stronger and different from disbelief at the price.
The verb stem plus gatai means psychologically hard to do; the price is hard to believe.
Zaru o enai means one cannot avoid believing, the opposite of saying the claim is hard to believe.

questions.questionText: こんな難しい本は売れないだろうという予想（　）、10万冊以上売れた。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】4（に反して）
「～に反して」⇒～と違って、～と反対に【ex】期待に反して／作者の意図に反して

studyExplanation.translation: Contrary to the prediction that such a difficult book would not sell, over 100,000 copies were sold.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: ni hanshite - contrary to or against

choices.reason: Ni taishite means toward or in contrast to something, but the fixed phrase for a result defying a prediction is ni hanshite.
Ni oujite means in response to or according to; sales exceeded rather than followed the forecast.
Ni atatte means on the occasion of; a prediction is not an occasion for the sales.
Ni hanshite marks a result opposite to an expectation or forecast.

questions.questionText: もう二度と失敗は（　）と思ったのに、またやってしまった。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】2（するものか）
「～ものか」⇒絶対～しない（強い否定の意志を表す）【ex】あんなところに行くものか。

studyExplanation.translation: I thought, 'I will never make that mistake again,' but then I did it again.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: suru mono ka - no way will I do it; a strong negative resolve

choices.reason: Mono da makes a general assertion that mistakes happen, rather than a determined refusal.
Mono ka is a forceful rhetorical denial: 'I will not do it again!'
Shinai mono da is a general claim that one does not do something, not the speaker's emphatic resolve.
Adding mono ka to a negative verb would rhetorically reject not doing it, reversing the intended resolve.

questions.questionText:
A「おひさしぶりです。」
B「本当に。（　）言えば、お父さまの病気はその後、いかがですか。」
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】3（そう）
「そう言えば」⇒話題を変えるときの決まり文句

studyExplanation.translation: A: 'It has been a long time.' B: 'It really has. Speaking of which, how has your father's illness been since then?'
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: sou ieba - speaking of which; used to introduce a related topic

choices.reason: Mou means already or more; mou ieba does not serve as this conversational topic-shift phrase.
Kou ieba means 'if I put it this way,' not 'speaking of which' when recalling a related topic.
Sou ieba is the fixed expression for remembering or bringing up something connected to the conversation.
Dou ieba would ask how to say something; it is not the set phrase introducing the father's condition.

questions.questionText: 私が結婚（　）がしまいが、あなたには関係ないことだ。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】3（しよう）
「～ようが～まいが」⇒～しても～しなくても【ex】このホテルでは朝食を食べようが食べまいが、お金は取られる。

studyExplanation.translation: Whether I get married or not is none of your business.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: shiyou ga shimai ga - whether one does it or not

choices.reason: Shitai means want to do it; the required pattern is volitional plus ga shimai ga, not desire plus ga.
Shita is past tense, but this fixed whether-or-not pattern calls for the volitional form.
Shiyou ga shimai ga means whether I do it or do not; marriage is irrelevant to the listener.
Shinai is negative and would duplicate the not-doing side of the paired pattern rather than oppose it.

questions.questionText: この薬の粒は大きすぎて、とても（　）。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】4（飲みにくい）
「動詞ます形 + にくい」⇒～することが難しい

studyExplanation.translation: These medicine tablets are too large and very difficult to swallow.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: nominikui - difficult to swallow

choices.reason: This means not to swallow too much, a statement about quantity rather than the difficulty caused by tablet size.
Kanenai means might well do something, not that swallowing is difficult.
Yasui means easy to swallow, the opposite of what the oversized tablets imply.
Nikui attached to the verb stem means difficult to do; large tablets are hard to swallow.

questions.questionText:
A「たばこを吸っても、必ず病気になるわけではないだろう。」
B「それでも医者にすれば、禁煙を（　）。」
options: 指導するわけがないよ
指導するどころではないよ
指導するはずがないよ
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】1（指導するしかないよ）
「動詞辞書形／名詞 + しかない」⇒～する以外に方法はない、～しなければならない

studyExplanation.translation: A: 'Smoking does not necessarily cause illness.' B: 'Even so, from a doctor's standpoint, there is nothing to do but advise people to quit smoking.'
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: shidou suru shika nai - have no choice but to advise

choices.reason: Shika nai means there is no alternative; a doctor must still advise smoking cessation despite uncertainty about outcomes.

choices.romaji: shidou suru wake ga nai yo
choices.reason: Wake ga nai denies any possibility of advising, opposite to the doctor's duty implied by 'even so.'

choices.romaji: shidou suru dokoro dewa nai yo
choices.reason: Dokoro dewa nai means one is in no position to advise, which conflicts with the doctor's role here.

choices.romaji: shidou suru hazu ga nai yo
choices.reason: Hazu ga nai says the doctor is not expected to advise, contrary to the conclusion of the dialogue.

questions.questionText: 会社の一駅前で降りて（　）、3カ月で体重がかなり減った。
options: 歩くようにしたものの
歩くようにしたところ
歩くようにしたものが
歩くようにしたところで
questions.correctOption: 歩くようにしたところ
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】2（歩くようにしたところ）
「～ところ…」⇒～という動作をした結果、…になる〈後に続く文は肯定、否定とも使う。【ex】抽選に申し込んだところ、当たった／はずれた。〉

studyExplanation.translation: When I started getting off one station before work and walking, I lost quite a lot of weight in three months.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: aruku you ni shita tokoro - when I made a habit of walking, the result was

choices.romaji: aruku you ni shita mono no
choices.reason: Mono no introduces a concession, as if the walking did not have the expected effect; the next clause reports a positive result.
Tokoro reports what happened as a result of trying the new walking habit: substantial weight loss.

choices.romaji: aruku you ni shita mono ga
choices.reason: Mono ga is not the result-reporting connector needed after this change of habit.

choices.romaji: aruku you ni shita tokoro de
choices.reason: Tokoro de means even if one does so, often implying futility; it does not introduce the observed weight-loss result.

questions.questionText: 会議に出席できなかったので、資料を（　）
options: お見せいただけますか
見られていただけますか
見せていただけますか
questions.correctOption: 見せていただけますか
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】4（見せていただけますか）
「～（さ）せていただく」⇒「自分が見る」という動作をへりくだって言っている。

studyExplanation.translation: I could not attend the meeting, so could you please let me see the materials?
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: misete itadakemasu ka - may I have you show them to me?

choices.reason: Omise is a humble form for one's own act of showing, but the speaker wants the other person to show the materials.
This combines the passive or potential form with itadaku incorrectly and does not ask to be shown the materials.
Mite itadaku asks someone else to look at something; the speaker needs to look at the meeting materials.
Misete itadaku politely requests that the other person show the materials so the speaker can see them.

questions.questionText: 難しい漢字は、習う＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ <u>　★　</u> ＿＿＿うちにきちんと復習しよう。
questions.instruction: 問題8　次の文の★に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】3（ので）
（難しい漢字は、習う）4 そばから 1 忘れてしまう 3 ので 2 忘れない（うちにきちんと復習しよう。）

studyExplanation.translation: Difficult kanji are forgotten as soon as they are learned, so review them properly before you forget them.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: node - because; star is third in 'soba kara, wasurete shimau, node, wasurenai'

choices.reason: This means 'end up forgetting' and belongs second after soba kara; placing it in the starred third slot leaves no cause connector.
This means 'not forget' and belongs fourth before uchi ni, creating 'before you forget.'
The order is 4-1-3-2. Node is third, at the star, linking immediate forgetting to the advice to review.
Soba kara follows 'learn' first and means 'as soon as'; it cannot occupy the third slot after the clause it introduces.

questions.questionText: 同じ言葉＿＿＿ <u>　★　</u> ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿印象が変わってしまうことがある。
questions.instruction: 問題8　次の文の★に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】4（話し方）
（同じ言葉）1 でも 4 話し方 3 次第 2 では（印象が変わってしまうことがある。）

studyExplanation.translation: Even with the same words, the impression can change depending on how they are said.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: hanashikata - way of speaking; star is second in 'demo, hanashikata, shidai, dewa'

choices.reason: Demo follows 'same words' first and means 'even'; it precedes the starred phrase about manner of speech.
Dewa belongs fourth after shidai to form 'depending on'; it cannot introduce hanashikata at the star.
Shidai follows hanashikata third, making 'depending on the way of speaking.'
The order is 1-4-3-2. Hanashikata is second, at the star, and names the way of speaking.

questions.questionText: この学校では、＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ <u>　★　</u> ＿＿＿で受けることができます。
questions.instruction: 問題8　次の文の★に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】2（限って）
（この学校では、）1 最初の 4 レッスンに 2 限って 3 無料（で受けることができます。）

studyExplanation.translation: At this school, you can take the first lesson for free, but only that lesson.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: kagitte - limited to; star is third in 'saisho no, ressun ni, kagitte, muryou'

choices.reason: This modifies 'lesson' in the first slot; the sentence singles out the first lesson.
The order is 1-4-2-3. Kagitte is third, at the star; ressun ni kagitte means limited to that lesson.
Muryou belongs fourth before de, yielding muryou de 'for free'; it is not the limiting phrase.
This follows saisho no second; the particle ni is required before kagitte.

questions.instruction: 問題8　次の文の★に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】1（の）
（この子は）3 年齢 1 の 2 わりには 4 ピアノ（が上手だ。）

studyExplanation.translation: For a child of this age, this child is remarkably good at the piano.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: no - possessive linker; star is second in 'nenrei, no, wari ni wa, piano'

choices.reason: The order is 3-1-2-4. No is second, at the star; nenrei no wari ni wa means 'considering the child's age.'
This follows nenrei no third, forming the 'considering/for' comparison; it cannot precede no.
Nenrei is first, providing the age used as the standard for the comparison.
Piano belongs fourth immediately before ga jouzu da, naming what the child plays well.

questions.questionText: あの学生の今までの＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ <u>　★　</u> ＿＿＿なんて信じられない。
questions.instruction: 問題8　次の文の★に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】3（こんな成績を）
（あの学生の今までの）2 成績から 4 見ても 3 こんな成績を 1 取る（なんて信じられない。）

studyExplanation.translation: Even judging by that student's previous grades, I cannot believe they would get grades like these.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: konna seiseki o - grades like these; star is third in 'seiseki kara, mite mo, konna seiseki o, toru'

choices.reason: Toru belongs fourth after the object 'grades like these'; it completes the phrase 'get these grades.'
This belongs first after 'previous,' giving the evidence from past grades for the judgment.
The order is 2-4-3-1. This object phrase is third, at the star, before toru.
Mite mo belongs second after kara, forming kara mite mo 'even judging from'; it is not the object of toru.

questions.instruction: 問題9　次の文章を読んで、文中に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.passage:
あなたは日本のすし屋のカウンターで、「お好み」ですしを食べたことがありますか。

カウンターのケースの中を見ながら、好きな魚を選び、それを注文して、にぎってもらうので、いちばんおいしい状態で食べられます。ただ自分がどれくらい食べたか、金額が［50］注意が必要です。

このとき、たとえば「マグロ」と注文すると、通常、マグロのすしが2つ出てきます。なぜそうなのか。江戸時代のおすしは大きかったので、2つに切って出したなごりとか、計算しやすくするためだとか、いろいろな説があります。結局、はっきりとはわからなくて、「昔からそうなっている」としか［51］。

ところで、この場合、［52-a］で行けば［52-b］食べればいいけれど、［52-c］で行って10個食べるとしたら、魚は5種類しか食べられません。ある回転ずし店で、1枚の皿に違う種類のすしを1つずつ2個、乗せ始めました。これなら、食べたすしの数だけ［53］が食べられるので人気が出て、客が増えたそうです。考えたら単純なアイデアです。でも「昔からそうなっている」ことをちょっと変えてみる、そこにお客が増えるかぎがありました。

私たちの身の回りにも、「ちょっと変えてみたらよくなる」ことがたくさんあるかもしれません。常識［54］、頭を柔らかくしておくことが大事なのです。

studyExplanation.translation: At a sushi counter you choose fish and eat it at its freshest, but you need to pay attention because it is hard to tell how much you have eaten and how much the bill will be.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: wakari-zurai node - because it is hard to tell

choices.reason: If the total were easy to understand, the warning to pay attention would lack a reason.
This means you end up understanding it, contrary to the concern about an uncertain bill.
Ordering piece by piece makes the total eaten and cost hard to track; the warning follows logically.
Kanenai means 'may well understand,' not 'difficult to understand,' so it reverses the intended reason.

options: 言いようがありません
言うまでもありません
questions.correctOption: 言いようがありません

studyExplanation.translation: Why does a single tuna order usually bring two pieces? There are several theories, but no definite answer; there is no way to say more than 'that is how it has always been.'

The lack of a definite explanation leaves no way to say anything beyond 'it has always been that way.'
Kanemasen means 'I am unable to say' in a refusal or difficulty, not the passage's fixed expression for no other explanation.

studyExplanation.translation: If two people go, each can eat one of the two sushi pieces, but if one person goes and eats ten pieces, that person can try only five kinds of fish.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: futari / ikko zutsu / hitori - two people / one each / one person

choices.reason: One person cannot split a standard two-piece order with a companion by eating one piece each.
One person cannot eat two pieces each, and the final five-kinds calculation concerns a solo diner, not two people.
Two diners can share each two-piece order one apiece; a solo diner eating ten pieces gets five two-piece fish orders.
If two diners each took two pieces per fish, that would require four pieces per type, not the usual pair described.

questions.passage:
あなたは日本のすし屋のカウンターで、「お好み」ですしを食べたことがありますか。

カウンターのケースの中を見ながら、好きな魚を選び、それを注文して、にぎってもらうので、いちばんおいしい状態で食べられます。ただ自分がどれくらい食べたか、金額が［50］注意が必要です。

このとき、たとえば「マグロ」と注文すると、通常、マグロのすしが2つ出てきます。なぜそうなのか。江戸時代のおすしは大きかったので、2つに切って出したなごりとか、計算しやすくするためだとか、いろいろな説があります。結局、はっきりとはわからなくて、「昔からそうなっている」としか［51］。

ところで、この場合、［52-a］で行けば［52-b］食べればいいけれど、［52-c］で行って10個食べるとしたら、魚は5種類しか食べられません。ある回転ずし店で、1枚の皿に違う種類のすしを1つずつ2個、乗せ始めました。これなら、食べたすしの数だけ［53］が食べられるので人気が出て、客が増えたそうです。考えたら単純なアイデアです。でも「昔からそうなっている」ことをちょっと変えてみる、そこにお客が増えるかぎがありました。

私たちの身の回りにも、「ちょっと変えてみたらよくなる」ことがたくさんあるかもしれません。常識［54］、頭を柔らかくしておくことが大事なのです。

studyExplanation.translation: The conveyor-belt sushi shop put two different kinds, one piece each, on a plate; customers could then eat as many different kinds of sushi as pieces they ate.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: iroiro na sushi - various kinds of sushi

choices.reason: The shop intentionally put two different kinds together, not the same kind.
The benefit is variety per number of pieces eaten, not simply eating a large quantity.
Customers need not eat every kind on the menu; the text discusses the number of varieties sampled.
One different kind per piece lets diners sample many varieties with fewer pieces.

questions.instruction: 問題9　次の文章を読んで、文中に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.passage:

カウンターのケースの中を見ながら、好きな魚を選び、それを注文して、にぎってもらうので、いちばんおいしい状態で食べられます。ただ自分がどれくらい食べたか、金額が［50］注意が必要です。

ところで、この場合、［52-a］で行けば［52-b］食べればいいけれど、［52-c］で行って10個食べるとしたら、魚は5種類しか食べられません。ある回転ずし店で、1枚の皿に違う種類のすしを1つずつ2個、乗せ始めました。これなら、食べたすしの数だけ［53］が食べられるので人気が出て、客が増えたそうです。考えたら単純なアイデアです。でも「昔からそうなっている」ことをちょっと変えてみる、そこにお客が増えるかぎがありました。

studyExplanation.translation: The shop's small change to the old two-piece custom attracted customers. Likewise, it is important to keep an open mind without being bound by conventional thinking.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: ni torawarenai de - without being constrained by

choices.reason: Not being bound by common sense matches the call to question long-standing customs and think flexibly.
Trying not to break conventions would preserve the old rule, contrary to the successful change in the story.
Avoiding involvement with common sense is not the intended idea; the problem is being constrained by it.
Leaving common sense entirely out is stronger and different from remaining flexible rather than captive to it.

sets.title: 第3回 模擬テスト
sets.description: 第3回　文字・語彙・文法

questions.questionText: ボランティア活動を<u>選択</u>科目に取り入れている大学が多くなっている。
questions.instruction: 問題1　下線の言葉の読み方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: More universities are incorporating volunteer activities into their elective courses.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 選択 (sentaku) - selection; an elective course

choices.reason: The second kanji 択 is read taku here, not daku; this voices the wrong syllable.
Both syllables are incorrectly voiced; 選択 begins with sen and ends with taku.
選択 is read sentaku; 選択科目 is an elective subject or course.
The ending taku is right, but 選 is sen, not zen, in 選択.

questions.questionText: 飛行場を建設するには<u>膨大</u>な費用がかかる。
questions.instruction: 問題1　下線の言葉の読み方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Constructing an airport requires an enormous amount of money.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 膨大 (boudai) - enormous or vast

choices.reason: 膨大 is read boudai and describes an enormous cost or quantity.
The first kanji 膨 is read bou in this word, not chou; choudai is not 膨大.
Bakudai is the reading of 莫大, another word for enormous, but the printed word is 膨大.
The first kanji is not read jin; 膨大 begins with bou.

questions.questionText: 軽く言ったつもりの<u>冗談</u>が友人を傷つけてしまった。
questions.instruction: 問題1　下線の言葉の読み方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: A joke that I thought I had made lightly ended up hurting my friend.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 冗談 (joudan) - joke

choices.reason: 冗 is voiced as jou in 冗談, not shou.
The first syllable is long: jou, not short jo.
談 is read dan, with a voiced d, not tan.
冗談 is read joudan and means a joke or joking remark.

questions.questionText: このまま人口が増え続ければ、世界中で食糧や水の<u>奪い</u>合いになるであろう。
questions.instruction: 問題1　下線の言葉の読み方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: If the population keeps increasing like this, people around the world will probably end up fighting over food and water.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 奪い合い (ubaiai) - struggle or competition to take something from one another

choices.reason: Kisoi corresponds to 競い, meaning competition; the printed verb 奪う is read ubau.
奪い is ubai, from 奪う (ubau); 奪い合い means a struggle over a limited resource.
Arasoi means a dispute and is written 争い, not 奪い.
Ukagai comes from 伺う, to inquire or visit; it is not the reading of 奪い.

questions.questionText: 最近は防犯<u>性能</u>が高いマンションや住宅を作るさまざまな取り組みが進んでいる。
questions.instruction: 問題1　下線の言葉の読み方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Recently, various efforts have been advancing to build apartments and homes with strong crime-prevention capabilities.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 性能 (seinou) - performance or functional capability

choices.reason: 性 is read sei in 性能, not zei.
Neither syllable matches the standard reading of 性能, seinou.
性 is not read suu here; 防犯性能 refers to security performance.
性能 is read seinou; 防犯性能 is the effectiveness of crime-prevention features.

questions.questionText: あのコーチは選手の<u>かくれた</u>能力を引き出すのがうまい。
questions.instruction: 問題2　下線の言葉を漢字で書くとき、最もよいものを1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: That coach is good at bringing out the players' hidden abilities.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 隠れた (kakureta) - hidden or latent

choices.reason: 隠れる means to be hidden; 隠れた能力 is a hidden ability.
陰 means shade or shadow, but 陰れた is not the standard spelling of kakureta.
隆 means flourishing or rising; 隆れた does not spell kakureta.
隔 means to separate; 隔れた is not the standard spelling of hidden.

questions.questionText: 火山灰は電気<u>けいとう</u>に入り込み、さまざまな誤作動を起こすことがある。
questions.instruction: 問題2　下線の言葉を漢字で書くとき、最もよいものを1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Volcanic ash can enter electrical systems and cause various malfunctions.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 系統 (keitou) - system or network

choices.reason: 計 relates to counting or planning; 計統 is not the compound for an electrical system.
形 means shape; 形統 does not mean a system.
系統 means a system or line; 電気系統 is the electrical system.
経 means passing through or managing, but 経統 is not the spelling of keitou here.

questions.questionText: これから先、都市の建築物はますます<u>こうそう</u>化が進むであろう。
questions.instruction: 問題2　下線の言葉を漢字で書くとき、最もよいものを1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: From now on, buildings in cities will probably become increasingly high-rise.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 高層 (kousou) - high-rise or multistory

choices.reason: 構想 means a plan or concept; 構想化 does not describe buildings growing taller.
高層 means high-rise; 高層化 means the shift toward taller buildings.
後送 means sending something back or to the rear, unrelated to building height.
効相 is not the compound for high-rise buildings; the intended kanji are 高層.

questions.questionText: 人間は一生悩むことから<u>かいほう</u>されないのだと思う。
questions.instruction: 問題2　下線の言葉を漢字で書くとき、最もよいものを1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: I think human beings are never freed from worrying throughout their lives.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 解放 (kaihou) - release or liberation

choices.reason: 倣 means to imitate; 解倣 is not the word for being freed from worries.
封 means to seal; 解封 would refer to unsealing, not liberation from worries.
報 means report or reward; 解報 is not the word meaning release.
解放される means to be released or freed; 悩むことから解放されない means never being free of worry.

questions.questionText: 野菜や果物の栄養価は昔のものと<u>くらべて</u>低くなっている。
questions.instruction: 問題2　下線の言葉を漢字で書くとき、最もよいものを1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: The nutritional value of vegetables and fruit has fallen compared with what it used to be.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 比べて (kurabete) - compared with

choices.reason: 並べて means arranging side by side, not making a comparison of nutritional value.
比べて is the te-form of 比べる, to compare; 昔のものと比べて means compared with earlier produce.
列べて is not the standard spelling of kurabete for comparison.
対べて is not the standard spelling; 比 is the kanji used in 比べる.

questions.questionText: （　）事情により今回のイベントは中止する。
questions.instruction: 問題3　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Due to various circumstances, this event will be canceled.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 諸事情 (shojijou) - various circumstances

choices.reason: 多 means many, but 多事情 is not the conventional compound in this notice.
複 means multiple or complex, but 複事情 is not the idiomatic expression.
重 means heavy or repeated, but 重事情 does not mean various circumstances.
諸 means various; 諸事情により is a standard formal phrase meaning due to various circumstances.

questions.questionText: 日曜日は家族で（　）帰りの旅行を楽しんだ。
questions.instruction: 問題3　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: On Sunday, the family enjoyed a day trip.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 日帰り (higaeri) - a day trip, returning the same day

choices.reason: 日帰り means returning on the same day; 日帰りの旅行 is a day trip.
泊 means an overnight stay, so 泊帰り is not the day-trip compound.
行 relates to going, but 行帰り is not the set expression for a trip without an overnight stay.
出 means going out; 出帰り is not the standard compound here.

questions.questionText: 道路工事は（　）年度から始まる。
questions.instruction: 問題3　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: The road construction will begin in the next fiscal year.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 来年度 (rainendo) - next fiscal or school year

choices.reason: 未 means not yet, but 未年度 is not the word for next fiscal year.
来年度 means the coming fiscal or school year, matching when construction is to start.
数 means several or number; 数年度 is not the standard expression for next year.
真 means true or real; 真年度 is not a time expression.

questions.questionText: 最新の機器を備えた近代（　）なビルが建設された。
questions.instruction: 問題3　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: A modern building equipped with the latest devices was constructed.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 近代的 (kindaiteki) - modern

choices.reason: 風 means style, but 近代風な is not the expected adjective in this sentence.
式 denotes a type or ceremony; 近代式な is not the intended adjectival form.
The suffix 的 forms the na-adjective 近代的な, meaning modern.
性 means nature or tendency; 近代性な does not form the adjective used here.

questions.questionText: 的確な質問をよくしてくる彼には将来（　）を感じる。
questions.instruction: 問題3　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: I see promise in him because he often asks precise questions.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 将来性 (shouraisei) - future potential or promise

choices.reason: 将来感 is not the usual compound for a person's future potential.
将来性を感じる means to sense that someone has future potential.
化 indicates a process of change; 将来化 is not a word for promise.
風 means style or manner; 将来風 is not the expression here.

questions.questionText: 試験の出来ですか。すごくよくはなかったけど（　）だったと思います。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: How did I do on the exam? It was not extremely good, but I think it was so-so.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: まあまあ (maa maa) - so-so or reasonably good

choices.reason: せいぜい means at most; it does not serve as the predicate せいぜいだった for this moderate assessment.
そろそろ means soon or about time, not an assessment of exam performance.
ゆうゆう means easily or leisurely, inconsistent with the speaker's modest evaluation.
まあまあだった says the result was passable or fairly good, fitting 'not extremely good.'

questions.questionText: 彼女を動物に（　）と、気まぐれなところがネコっぽいね。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: If you compared her to an animal, her fickle side would make her rather catlike.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 例える (tatoeru) - compare or liken to

choices.reason: 動物に例える means to liken someone to an animal; it introduces the cat comparison.
比べる means to compare two things, usually AとBを比べる, not to liken a person to an animal with に.
たたえる means to praise or extol, not to make an analogy.
こたえる means to answer or respond, unrelated to the catlike description.

questions.questionText: なんでもすぐ行動に移す彼は、気が短い人間だと（　）されている。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Because he acts on everything immediately, people mistakenly think he is an impatient person.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 誤解 (gokai) - misunderstanding or mistaking someone for something

choices.reason: 評判 is a reputation, but 評判されている is not the natural construction for being mistakenly regarded as impatient.
結論 means conclusion; 結論されている is not how one says people misjudge him.
気が短い人間だと誤解されている means he is misunderstood as being short-tempered.
決定 means decision; his personality is not being formally decided by others.

questions.questionText: 昔は貴族以外のまずしい人々は、小さくて（　）な家に住んでいた。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: In the past, poor people who were not aristocrats lived in small, humble houses.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 粗末 (somatsu) - shabby or humble

choices.reason: 不利 means disadvantageous, not a description of the physical condition of a house.
不幸 means unhappy or unfortunate; it does not naturally modify 家 as a house's quality.
地味 means plain or subdued, but the poor, small dwellings are described as 粗末, humble or shabby.
粗末な家 is a shabby or humble home, consistent with poverty in the sentence.

questions.questionText: 新入社員は、（　）な魅力にあふれている。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: New employees are full of fresh appeal.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: フレッシュ (furesshu) - fresh or youthful

choices.reason: オープン means open, but オープンな魅力 is not the intended description of new employees' fresh appeal.
フレッシュな魅力 expresses the youthful, new appeal associated with new employees.
ダイレクト means direct; ダイレクトな魅力 does not convey the newness emphasized by 新入社員.
ショック means a shock and does not form the natural description ショックな魅力.

questions.questionText: この運動靴は歩きやすさとデザインのよさを（　）備えている。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: These sneakers combine ease of walking with a good design.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 兼ね備えている (kanesonaete iru) - possess both qualities

choices.reason: 持ち備える is not the idiomatic compound for having two qualities at once.
造り備える is not a natural verb; 造る concerns making or building.
取り備える is not the set compound for combining qualities.
兼ね備える means to possess both; here the shoes have comfort and good design.

questions.questionText: この商店街で生活（　）はすべてそろう。
questions.instruction: 問題4　（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: Everything needed for daily life is available in this shopping district.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 生活必需品 (seikatsu hitsujuhin) - daily necessities

choices.reason: 季節品 would mean seasonal goods, not all essentials for everyday living.
生活必需品 is the fixed compound for items necessary in daily life.
付属品 are accessories or attachments, not everyday necessities.
消耗品 are consumables; the sentence refers more broadly to daily necessities.

questions.questionText: 姉はいらないものまで<u>やたらに</u>買い込んでしまう。
questions.instruction: 問題5　下線の言葉に意味が最も近いものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: My older sister indiscriminately buys even things she does not need.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 考えなしに (kangae nashi ni) - without thinking or indiscriminately

choices.reason: やたらに means recklessly or indiscriminately, so 'without thinking' fits buying unnecessary things.
思いっきり means with all one's might or to one's heart's content, not necessarily without judgment.
絶えず means continually; frequency alone does not express やたらに's lack of restraint.
大量に means in large quantities; quantity is not the same as indiscriminate buying.

questions.questionText: 彼女は<u>隙</u>のない人だ。
questions.instruction: 問題5　下線の言葉に意味が最も近いものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: She is a person who never lets her guard down.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 油断 (yudan) - carelessness or letting one's guard down

choices.reason: 余裕 means room or composure; 隙がない here means no vulnerable opening, not no spare capacity.
夢 means dream, unrelated to 隙, an opening or lapse.
隙のない describes someone who leaves no opening; 油断 is the lapse or carelessness such a person avoids.
特徴 means characteristic; it does not convey an unguarded opening.

questions.questionText: 新しい法案作りを<u>慎重に</u>進める。
questions.instruction: 問題5　下線の言葉に意味が最も近いものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: They are proceeding carefully with drafting a new bill.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 注意深く (chuui bukaku) - carefully or attentively

choices.reason: 容易に means easily, not with caution.
計画的に means systematically or according to a plan; that is not the same as 慎重に, cautiously.
注意深く means attentively and carefully, matching 慎重に when preparing a bill.
素早く means quickly, which says nothing about carefulness.

questions.questionText: 事故を起こした会社の社長はマスコミに<u>叩かれた</u>。
questions.instruction: 問題5　下線の言葉に意味が最も近いものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: The president of the company that caused the accident was criticized by the media.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 非難された (hinan sareta) - was criticized or condemned

choices.reason: 質問された means was questioned; 叩かれた here implies hostile criticism, not merely questions.
称賛された means was praised, the opposite of the negative media response.
注目された means attracted attention; 叩かれた is specifically critical attention.
In this media context, 叩かれた figuratively means was attacked or condemned in public.

questions.questionText: このギターは限定生産の<u>レアな</u>ものだ。
questions.instruction: 問題5　下線の言葉に意味が最も近いものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。

studyExplanation.translation: This guitar is a rare, limited-production item.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: めずらしい (mezurashii) - rare or unusual

choices.reason: 新しい means new; a limited-production item can be rare without being new.
レア means rare; limited production explains why this guitar is unusual.
高い means expensive; rarity does not by itself state the price.
すばらしい means excellent; the sentence emphasizes scarcity, not quality.

questions.questionText: 恩恵
options: この祭りは自然の<u>恩恵</u>に浴する感謝を表している。
お世話になった人に<u>恩恵</u>返しをする。
この神社のお守りは<u>恩恵</u>があると評判だ。
先生の<u>恩恵</u>で、無事卒業することができた。
questions.correctOption: この祭りは自然の<u>恩恵</u>に浴する感謝を表している。
questions.instruction: 問題6　次の言葉の使い方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation: 【正解】1（この祭りは自然の<u>恩恵</u>に浴する感謝を表している。）

studyExplanation.translation: This festival expresses gratitude for receiving the blessings of nature.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 恩恵 (onkei) - benefit or blessing bestowed on someone

choices.reason: 自然の恩恵に浴する means to enjoy or receive nature's benefits; this is the appropriate use of 恩恵.
Returning a personal favor is 恩返し, not 恩恵返し; 恩恵 names a benefit received.
A shrine amulet may have ご利益, a blessing or efficacy, but 恩恵がある is not the intended amulet expression.
For being able to graduate thanks to a teacher, おかげで is natural; 先生の恩恵で is not the intended usage here.

questions.questionText: <ruby>素人<rt>しろうと</rt></ruby>
options: 税金が上がって、<u>素人</u>の生活は苦しくなった。
これはとても<u>素人</u>には作れない料理だ。
どこの<u>素人</u>かわからない男に娘を嫁にやるわけにはいかない。
彼女は<u>素人</u>だけあって、とても美しい。
questions.correctOption: これはとても<u>素人</u>には作れない料理だ。
questions.instruction: 問題6　次の言葉の使い方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation: 【正解】2（これはとても<u>素人</u>には作れない料理だ。）

studyExplanation.translation: This is a dish that an amateur could never make.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 素人 (shirouto) - amateur or nonexpert

choices.reason: The intended group affected by higher taxes is ordinary people, not necessarily amateurs; 素人 contrasts with experts.
素人には作れない contrasts an amateur's skills with those required for this dish.
For an unknown man as a marriage prospect, どこの誰だかわからない fits; 素人 describes expertise, not identity.
Being very beautiful is not a consequence of being 素人, an amateur; the causal だけあって is misplaced.

questions.questionText: だらしない
options: 夫に家事を手伝ってもらったが、ちょっと<u>だらしない</u>。
こんなつまらない仕事、<u>だらしなくて</u>やっていられない。
そんなことで落ちこむなんて、<u>だらしない</u>やつだ。
彼女はきちんと家計簿をつけていて、とてもお金に<u>だらしない</u>。
questions.correctOption: そんなことで落ちこむなんて、<u>だらしない</u>やつだ。
questions.instruction: 問題6　次の言葉の使い方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation: 【正解】3（そんなことで落ちこむなんて、<u>だらしない</u>やつだ。）

studyExplanation.translation: What a spineless person to get discouraged by something like that.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: だらしない (darashinai) - spineless, sloppy or undisciplined

choices.reason: A poor job of helping with housework would be いい加減 or 雑; だらしない alone does not describe the work naturally here.
For work that is too dull to continue, つまらなくて fits; だらしない describes conduct or self-discipline.
だらしない can criticize lack of resolve; giving up over something minor makes the person seem spineless.
Keeping careful household accounts indicates discipline with money, the opposite of お金にだらしない.

questions.questionText: 重点
options: 日本では、話すことより読む勉強に<u>重点</u>を置く学校がいまだ多い。
この計画の成功の<u>重点</u>は君の活躍にかかっている。
彼は長年財界の<u>重点</u>だった。
あの作家の<u>重点</u>のある言葉が気に入っている。
questions.correctOption: 日本では、話すことより読む勉強に<u>重点</u>を置く学校がいまだ多い。
questions.instruction: 問題6　次の言葉の使い方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation: 【正解】1（日本では、話すことより読む勉強に<u>重点</u>を置く学校がいまだ多い。）

studyExplanation.translation: Even now, many schools in Japan place more emphasis on reading than on speaking.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 重点を置く (juuten o oku) - place emphasis on

choices.reason: 重点を置く is the fixed expression for placing emphasis on something, here reading study.
The key to a plan's success is 鍵 or 重要な点, not 成功の重点.
An influential figure in business is 重鎮, not 重点; 重点 means emphasis or focus.
Words may have weight or substance, 重み, but 重点のある言葉 is not the intended expression.

questions.questionText: 支給
options: このコース修了者には資格を<u>支給</u>する。
客は店員に品物の代金を現金で<u>支給</u>した。
海外旅行をするなら旅券の<u>支給</u>手続きをしてください。
この会社は、給料のほかに家族手当が<u>支給</u>される。
questions.correctOption: この会社は、給料のほかに家族手当が<u>支給</u>される。
questions.instruction: 問題6　次の言葉の使い方として最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation: 【正解】4（この会社は、給料のほかに家族手当が<u>支給</u>される。）

studyExplanation.translation: At this company, family allowances are paid in addition to salary.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 支給される (shikyuu sareru) - be provided or paid out

choices.reason: A qualification is granted or awarded, 資格を与える, rather than 支給する, which supplies money or goods.
A customer pays a shopkeeper, 支払う; 支給する is not used for a retail payment.
A passport is issued, 旅券の発給, not 支給; the latter is for funds or supplies.
Family allowances are monetary benefits a company pays out; 手当が支給される is natural.

questions.questionText: いったん仕事を引き受けた（　）、何があっても完成させなければならない。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】4（上は）
「～上は」⇒～からには〈後の文に決意、意志を表す文が続く。〉

studyExplanation.translation: Now that I have accepted the job, I must finish it no matter what happens.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 上は (ue wa) - now that; since one has committed to doing it

choices.reason: 上から means from above or from the point of view of; it does not express the obligation following acceptance.
上で after a past verb means after doing something; it does not itself convey the resolve 'now that I have accepted it.'
上に means in addition to; the second clause is not an added fact about accepting the job.
Verb-past plus 上は means now that a decision is made; it naturally leads to the firm obligation 完成させなければならない.

questions.questionText: 財布を忘れたが、クレジットカードを持っていた（　）、何とか買い物ができた。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】4（おかげで）
「～おかげで」⇒～という理由のため（…というよい結果になった）

studyExplanation.translation: I forgot my wallet, but thanks to having a credit card, I managed to shop anyway.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: おかげで (okage de) - thanks to; because of a favorable cause

choices.reason: せいで blames a cause for a bad result, but being able to shop is a favorable result.
くせに means despite or even though, often with reproach; it does not credit the card for helping.
ものの means although; it marks contrast, not the helpful cause of being able to shop.
持っていたおかげで identifies the credit card as the reason the speaker could still make purchases.

questions.questionText: けちな彼女（　）、本物のダイヤモンドなんか買うはずがない。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】2（のことだから）
「ある人物 + のことだから」⇒ある人の性格や習慣を知っていて、次の行動を推量する【ex】お父さんのことだから、きっとすごく怒るよ。

studyExplanation.translation: Knowing how stingy she is, she would never buy a real diamond.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: のことだから (no koto dakara) - knowing that person's character

choices.reason: のことから is not the pattern used to predict someone's behavior from a known personality trait.
彼女のことだから uses her known stinginess to infer that she would not buy a real diamond.
のこととはいえ means even though it concerns that person; it does not make the character-based inference.
のことにしては is not the grammatical pattern for this prediction; にしては usually marks an unexpected contrast.

questions.questionText: A社はライバルだが、条件（　）は<ruby>合併<rt>がっぺい</rt></ruby>の<ruby>交渉<rt>こうしょう</rt></ruby>をしてもよい。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】2（次第では）
「～次第では」⇒～という条件や意向によっては【ex】給料次第ではアルバイトをしてもいい。

studyExplanation.translation: Company A is a rival, but depending on the terms, we could negotiate a merger.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 次第では (shidai de wa) - depending on the conditions

choices.reason: 以前では means before, not depending on the proposed merger terms.
条件次第では means if the conditions allow it; this determines whether merger talks are possible.
程度では means at that degree or level; it does not express a conditional decision based on terms.
事情では refers to circumstances but is not the fixed pattern 条件次第では.

questions.questionText: 大地震（　）、地図で家までの帰り道を確認しておこう。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】3（に備えて）
「～に備えて」⇒ある事態が起きたときのために準備する【ex】病気に備えて保険に入る。

studyExplanation.translation: In preparation for a major earthquake, let's check the route home on a map.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: に備えて (ni sonaete) - in preparation for

choices.reason: に応じて means in response to or according to; the quake has not happened yet.
に向かって means toward; checking a map is not movement toward an earthquake.
大地震に備えて means preparing for a possible major earthquake in advance.
に関して means concerning; it does not express the purpose of advance preparation.

questions.questionText: 「さくらが咲いた」とニュースになるくらい、日本の春はさくら（　）語れない。
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】2（ぬきには）
「～ぬきには」⇒～がなくては【ex】現代生活はコンピューターぬきには考えられない。

studyExplanation.translation: In Japan, cherry blossoms are so central to spring that even their blooming makes the news; you cannot talk about spring without them.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: ぬきには (nuki ni wa) - without; not apart from

choices.reason: だけでは means with only; さくらだけでは語れない would say blossoms alone are insufficient, the opposite emphasis.
さくらぬきには語れない means spring cannot be discussed without mentioning cherry blossoms.
ほどには means not to the extent of; it does not form the 'cannot do without' pattern.
のみでは means with only; like だけでは, it does not say blossoms are indispensable.

questions.questionText:
A「もしもし、山下社長はいらっしゃいますか。」
B「ただいま、席を（　）、折り返しご連絡差し上げます。」
options: はずされておりますので
はずしていらっしゃいますので
はずしておりますので
はずしてしまいますので
questions.correctOption: はずしておりますので
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】3（はずしておりますので）
自分の会社の社長であっても外部の人に対しては謙譲語を使う。「席をはずす」⇒「その人の席にいない」決まり文句として覚えること。

studyExplanation.translation: Caller: Hello, is President Yamashita available? Staff member: He is away from his desk at the moment, so I will have him call you back.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 席をはずしておりますので (seki o hazushite orimasu node) - he is away from his desk, so...

choices.reason: はずされております is passive, as though someone removed him from the seat; the idiom is 席をはずす.
はずしていらっしゃいます uses honorific language for one's own company president to an outside caller; the printed explanation requires humble language.
席をはずしております is the polite, humble form used by company staff when speaking to an outside caller about their own president.
はずしてしまいます suggests he will leave or has unfortunately left, not that he is currently away from his desk.

questions.questionText: 急いで論文を書いているが、このままでは締め切りには（　）。
options: 間に合わないはずがない
間に合うわけでもない
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】1（間に合いそうもない）
「動詞ます形 + そうもない」⇒～する様子がない〈非常に可能性の低いことを表す。【ex】雨は降りそうもない。／だれも来そうにない。〉

studyExplanation.translation: I am writing the paper in a hurry, but at this rate it does not look as though I will meet the deadline.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 間に合いそうもない (maniai sou mo nai) - unlikely to make it in time

choices.reason: The masu-stem plus そうもない expresses that meeting the deadline appears very unlikely.
間に合わないはずがない means there is no way I will fail to make it, contrary to このままでは.
間に合うわけでもない only says it is not necessarily true that I will make it; it misses the strong negative outlook.
間に合うほかない means there is no alternative but to make it, not that success looks unlikely.

questions.questionText: 私がここの決まりを（　）、みなさんにご迷惑をおかけしました。
options: 知らなかったばかりに
questions.correctOption: 知らなかったばかりに
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】4（知らなかったばかりに）
「～ばかりに」⇒～という行動をしたために（悪い結果になった）【ex】よそ見をしたばかりに車をぶつけた。

studyExplanation.translation: Just because I did not know the rules here, I caused everyone trouble.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 知らなかったばかりに (shiranakatta bakari ni) - solely because I did not know

choices.reason: 知っていただけに means precisely because I knew, usually followed by a contrast; the speaker did not know the rules.
知らなかっただけに means all the more because I did not know; the printed causal pattern for the bad outcome is ばかりに.
知っていたばかりに blames knowing the rules, contradicting the intended cause.
ばかりに marks a cause that produced an undesirable outcome: the speaker's ignorance inconvenienced others.

questions.questionText: あなたがしゃべらない限り、このことを知っている（　）。
options: 人がいるということだ
人がいないということだ
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】2（人はいないはずだ）
「～ない限り…ない」⇒…（である）ためには～（する）しかない

studyExplanation.translation: Unless you speak up, there should be no one who knows about this.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 人はいないはずだ (hito wa inai hazu da) - there should be no one

choices.reason: 人がいるはずだ says somebody must know, opposite to the condition 'unless you speak.'
しゃべらない限り means unless you speak; with no other source of disclosure, no one should know.
人がいるということだ asserts that someone knows, contrary to the conditional secrecy.
人がいないということだ reports a conclusion as fact; はずだ expresses the expected result of the condition more naturally.

questions.questionText: 食べ物は新鮮であればあるほど（　）、少し古いほうがおいしい食品もある。
options: おいしいわけではなく
おいしくないわけではなく
questions.correctOption: おいしいわけではなく
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】2（おいしいわけではなく）
「普通は新鮮なほうがおいしいが、そうでないものもある（部分否定）」という意味を表す。

studyExplanation.translation: Food is not necessarily tastier the fresher it is; some foods taste better when they are a little older.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: おいしいわけではなく (oishii wake de wa naku) - it is not necessarily tasty

choices.reason: おいしいはずで says it should be tasty, leaving no room for the contrast that some older foods taste better.
わけではない gives a partial negation: freshness does not always guarantee better taste.
おいしくないはずで predicts fresher food should not taste good, opposite to the usual expectation in the first clause.
おいしくないわけではなく says it is not necessarily bad, which does not directly negate 'fresher is tastier.'

questions.questionText: 現代の日本では、長男だからといって必ず家を（　）。
options: つがないではいられない
questions.instruction: 問題7　次の文の（　）に入れるのに最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】1（つぐわけではない）
「～からといって…ない」⇒～という原因・理由でも、全部同じ…という結果にならない

studyExplanation.translation: In modern Japan, being the eldest son does not necessarily mean that you will take over the family line or business.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: つぐわけではない (tsugu wake de wa nai) - does not necessarily inherit or succeed

choices.reason: だからといって with わけではない rejects the claim that every eldest son must succeed the family.
つがないではいられない says one cannot help succeeding, which would imply compulsion.
ついではならない means must not take over, a prohibition not stated in the sentence.
つがざるを得ない means have no choice but to succeed, the opposite of the partial negation.

questions.questionText: あなたが困って ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ <u>　★　</u> ＿＿＿ あげたいのだが……。
questions.instruction: 問題8　次の文の★に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】2（しては）
（あなたが困って）3 いるなら 4 私と 2 しては 1 助けて（あげたいのだが……。）

studyExplanation.translation: If you are having trouble, I would like to help you, for my part, but...
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: しては (shite wa) - as for, in the phrase 私としては at the marked third blank

choices.reason: 助けて (tasukete) connects to あげたい, 'want to help you'; it is the fourth fragment, not the starred third one.
The complete order is いるなら, 私と, しては, 助けて. 私としては means 'as far as I am concerned'; しては fills the starred third blank.
いるなら (iru nara) completes 困っているなら, 'if you are in trouble'; it belongs first.
私と (watashi to) begins 私としては and follows 困っているなら; it belongs second, immediately before the star.

questions.questionText: 私の妻は ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ <u>　★　</u> ＿＿＿ で高い服を買うことがある。
questions.instruction: 問題8　次の文の★に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】3（一方で）
（私の妻は）2 10円を 4 節約する 3 一方で 1 平気（で高い服を買うことがある。）

studyExplanation.translation: My wife saves even ten yen on the one hand, yet sometimes buys expensive clothes without a second thought.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 一方で (ippou de) - while, on the other hand, at the marked third blank

choices.reason: 平気 (heiki) combines with the printed で to make 平気で, 'without hesitation'; it is the fourth fragment.
10円を (juu-en o) is the object of 節約する, 'save ten yen'; it is the first fragment.
The complete order is 10円を, 節約する, 一方で, 平気. 節約する一方で contrasts her thrift with expensive shopping; 一方で is the starred third fragment.
節約する (setsuyaku suru) completes 10円を節約する and stands before 一方で, in the second blank.

questions.questionText: この店のケーキは ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ <u>　★　</u> ＿＿＿ も人気がある。
questions.instruction: 問題8　次の文の★に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】1（もちろん）
（この店のケーキは）2 甘すぎないので 3 女性は 1 もちろん 4 男性に（も人気がある。）

studyExplanation.translation: Because this shop's cakes are not too sweet, they are popular with men as well as women.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: もちろん (mochiron) - of course; part of 'not only women but also men' at the star

choices.reason: The order is 甘すぎないので, 女性は, もちろん, 男性に. 女性はもちろん男性にも means 'not only with women but with men too'; もちろん is the third, starred fragment.
甘すぎないので (amasuginai node) gives the reason the cakes appeal broadly; it belongs first.
女性は (josei wa) begins the paired phrase 女性はもちろん男性にも, so it is second, before the star.
男性に (dansei ni) takes the printed も to make 男性にも, 'also among men'; it is fourth.

questions.questionText: 時間にだらしない山下さんの ＿＿＿ <u>　★　</u> ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ でさぼっているのだろう。
questions.instruction: 問題8　次の文の★に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】4（だから）
（時間にだらしない山下さんの）1 こと 4 だから 2 また 3 どこか（でさぼっているのだろう。）

studyExplanation.translation: Knowing how careless Yamashita is about time, he is probably slacking off somewhere again.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: だから (dakara) - because of; completing 山下さんのことだから at the star

choices.reason: こと (koto) completes 山下さんのこと, 'knowing Yamashita'; it is the first fragment.
また (mata) means again and modifies the suspected repeated slacking; it belongs after だから, in the third blank overall after the star.
どこか (dokoka) means somewhere and combines with the printed で, forming どこかで; it is last.
The complete order is こと, だから, また, どこか. 山下さんのことだから draws an inference from his known habit; だから is the starred second blank.

questions.questionText: 人の ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ <u>　★　</u> ＿＿＿、その先にイベント会場があった。
questions.instruction: 問題8　次の文の★に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.explanation:
【正解】3（沿って）
（人の）4 歩く 1 流れに 3 沿って 2 進むと（、その先にイベント会場があった。）

studyExplanation.translation: When I followed the flow of people walking, the event venue was farther ahead.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: 沿って (sotte) - following or along; the starred third fragment

choices.reason: 流れに (nagare ni) means 'to/along the flow' and follows 人の歩く; it is second, not starred.
進むと (susumu to) means 'when I went forward' and follows 沿って; it is the fourth fragment.
The complete order is 歩く, 流れに, 沿って, 進むと. 人の歩く流れに沿って進むと means 'when I went along the flow of people walking'; 沿って is starred.
歩く (aruku) modifies 流れ, forming 'the flow of people walking'; it belongs first.

questions.instruction: 問題9　次の文章を読んで、文中に入る最もよいものを、1・2・3・4から一つ選びなさい。
questions.passage:
妻と離別りべつ、または死別しべつして20歳以下の子どもを育てている男性の家庭を「父子家庭ふしかてい」と言います（これに対し、母親と児童の家庭を「母子ぼし家庭」と言います）。最近の20年、離婚の増加により父子家庭の数は過去最高になりました。

母子家庭には、その収入［50］、児童扶養手当じどうふようてあてという子どもを育てるためのお金が支給しきゅうされ、ほかにもさまざまな制度があります。日本は「夫が外でお金を稼ぎ、妻が家庭で家事・育児をする」という考えが強かったので、［51-a］は経済的に苦しい家が多かったためです。

一方、「［51-b］と比べて［51-c］には経済的な問題はないだろう」と思われていたので、児童扶養手当は支給されていませんでした。

ところが父子家庭の収入は、母子家庭ほど［52］、平均に比べたらずいぶん低いことがわかりました。［53］、日本では男性は長い残業も休日出勤もやるのが当たり前で、「保育園に子どもを迎えに行くから、5時には帰らなければならない」という男性を雇やとってくれる会社は、あまり多くないのです。すでに働いていても、正社員でなくアルバイトになったり、男性であっても、［54］。

そして、厚生労働省こうせいろうどうしょうは低収入の父子家庭にも児童扶養手当を支給することを決定しました。この制度は2010年の年末から施行しこうされることになり、約10万所帯が給付きゅうふの対象になります。

studyExplanation.translation: Single-mother households receive a child-rearing allowance according to their income, along with other forms of support.
studyExplanation.correctAnswerEnglish: に応じた (ni oujita) - according to or corresponding to income

choices.reason: に伴った (ni tomonatta) means accompanying a change or event; the allowance amount is tied to the income level.
収入に応じた means adjusted according to income; it modifies the child-rearing allowance paid to single-mother households.
に比べた (ni kurabeta) means compared with; no second income is being compared in this clause.
に沿った (ni sotta) means in line with a policy or path, not calibrated to household income.
